newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler fights for new EU rural/farm policy.
newsitem.headline: Fischler fights for new EU rural/farm policy.

text.p: Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler fought on Monday to save plans for an integrated rural development policy, rejecting claims that there was widespread opposition.
"It was not a rejection by the Dublin EU summit, only that several questions needed further discussion," Fischler told the European Parliament's agriculture committee.
These included the impact on the EU's Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) and funding of the new rural policy.
Many member states, including Germany and France, are concerned that it would drain funds away from farmers.
Fischler denied that only Britain and Sweden supported the policy launched at a conference in Cork, Ireland, in November.
"I couldn't say that only two member states were in favour and the others were sceptical. It needs more discussion," he said.
The Cork Declaration called for further farm reforms to prepare for the next round of world trade negotiations starting in 1999 and the EU's enlargement eastwards early next century.

Fischler argued that it made sense to have a single source of funding, instead of three at present -- European Agricultural Guidance and Guarantee Fund, Regional and Social -- to save rural jobs and guarantee a future in the regions.
